question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?
answer:
Student Accounts handles refunds. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. [1] The threshold is $1.00 or greater for a Title IV aid overpayment and $5.00 for non-Title IV aid. [1]

You don’t have to sign up for direct deposit: it is a free option that deposits the refund to your checking or savings account. [1] To enroll: [3]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/.
2. Locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup.
3. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
4. In My Profile, click Payment Profile. Edit an existing payment method or create one, then check the box in Refund Option to designate it for direct deposit.

Direct-deposit refunds are expected within one to two weeks after submitting the application, for students eligible for a refund due to loan or financial-aid overpayment or dropping classes within the appropriate add/drop dates. [2] Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495; D-Wing, First Floor. [2]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/)

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
After the published withdrawal deadline, a student may NOT withdraw from a course [3]. The deadline is on the [Academic Calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/). The catalog describes a possible late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: ordinarily apply before the semester ends; explain why standard withdrawal procedures could not be followed and identify the term. Typically, approval means W grades for all courses in that term, and ordinarily only one term per appeal. Documentation may include medical records, a death certificate, proof of required family caregiving, disaster-relocation documentation, or an employer’s dated relocation letter. The Provost or designee decides; the burden of proof is on the student [2, 5].

Withdrawing may affect financial aid and progress toward graduation [1]. For a withdrawal from any classes, Financial Aid recommends discussing the impact on your current aid package with its office [6, 10]. If withdrawing leaves you with fewer than 6 credits, federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ state aid requires full-time enrollment when fully disbursed [10]. Students who officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of the semester ends are subject to Title IV aid return rules; the amount is based on the percentage of the term attended, and repayment may be required [9].

SAP is reviewed annually after spring. Standards include completing at least 67% of attempted credits, undergraduate GPA of at least 2.0 or graduate GPA of 3.0, and staying within 150% of the program’s published length [7]. The pages do not determine your individual aid or SAP outcome.

Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [3]. Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [2]. Financial Aid: finaid@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7549, E-210 [6, 7, 9, 10].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/)

question: I got a parking ticket yesterday because my permit was still processing. how do I appeal it and who do I email

The pages differ on how to submit: section 1 says appeals are accepted through citation@ramapo.edu; section 2 says to enter appeals online via the form at https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3 [1, 2]. question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost
answer:
Apply online: the Student Accounts page links to the parking registration portal [1,2]; Public Safety also links to the registration portal [6,8]. The pages give different application instructions: section 10 says use ThePermitStore.com, enter Ramapo as your parking destination, then follow the steps for personal information, permit, vehicle, and payment (which should say “No Payment Necessary”); finish, print the temporary permit, and activate the mailed permit through your account. Section 11 instead directs you to RCNJ Parking Permits: choose permit type, enter contact and vehicle information, review and submit, then save or print the registration confirmation (which is not the permit). Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and “student,” not “faculty/staff” [10,11].
Public Safety says the fee is applied to your term bill before you visit the permit page [7]; it automatically appears on the bill [1,9]. Permit pickup instructions in section 7 say new students pick up at New Student Check-In, returning residents at their on-campus mailbox, and returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours. For another pickup time, email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu and request it; after 3 pm, pick up at the Public Safety Office Main Desk [7]. This differs from section 10, which says the temporary permit is printed and the permanent one arrives by mail [10].
For 2026–2027, the fee list contains the incomplete entry “student) | $125.00”; its label is cut off. It also lists Spring-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge $8.29, Spring-only Resident Parking Supplement $25.00, Summer-only Parking Permit $100.00, and Summer-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge $6.63 [5]. Off-campus students are charged 6.63% New Jersey sales tax on parking fees; on-campus students are exempt [1]. The parking fee is billed automatically; if you will not park on campus at any time during the school year, submit a Parking Fee Waiver Form to Student Accounts. A waiver is not processed if you have applied for a permit [9].
